name: semantic-preserving bounded segmentation with capped crosscheck redundancy
purpose: Predefine how the historical evidence corpus is segmented and how large evaluator batches may be before any evaluator sees raw evidence. The lead evaluator may choose semantic grouping and crosscheck selection only within these fixed bounds.

heuristic.principle: Create small stable evidence units that preserve local meaning, then group them into bounded batches sized to keep a single evaluator request far below the model's input-token-per-minute ceiling.
preferred_boundary_order: JSON array/object member boundary when recoverable without changing source text
hard UTF-8 byte boundary only as a last resort
justification: File-level assignment previously allowed individual evaluator contexts to become pathologically large.
Approximately 120 KB segments are small enough to redistribute semantically while usually preserving multi-record local context.
A 240 KB primary-batch target keeps a fresh evaluator request materially below the earlier megabyte-scale requests that exhausted the 2,000,000 input-token/minute quota.
A 320 KB hard primary ceiling allows limited bin-packing slack without permitting a batch to grow back toward megabyte scale.
Crosscheck batches are smaller because they are redundant evidence passes rather than primary coverage.
Base segmentation contains no overlap; every repeated raw byte is explicit crosscheck cost and is counted against the global redundancy budget.

batch_constraints.primary_batch_count_rule: The planner must produce at least ceil(D / target_primary_batch_bytes) primary batches and may produce more when semantic grouping or hard batch limits require it.
batch_constraints.primary_batch_size_rule: No primary batch may exceed hard_max_primary_batch_bytes.
batch_constraints.crosscheck_batch_size_rule: No crosscheck batch may exceed hard_max_crosscheck_batch_bytes.
batch_constraints.crosscheck_rule: Crosscheck batches may intentionally overlap or redistribute already-primary-assigned segments, including deterministic or seeded stochastic selection, but all repeated raw bytes count against the extra 0.5D redundancy budget.

fresh_evaluator_isolation.rule: Every planner, primary batch, crosscheck batch, and final synthesis evaluation is executed in a newly instantiated Node process and a new Gemini request.
fresh_evaluator_isolation.batch_input_rule: A batch evaluator receives only the common audit instruction plus the materialized raw segments assigned to that one batch. It receives no other batch raw context, no previous model conversation, and no previous batch result.
fresh_evaluator_isolation.synthesis_input_rule: The synthesis evaluator receives compact batch results and the validated plan, but no raw historical corpus.

evaluation_pipeline: fresh lead planner groups fixed segment IDs into primary batches and crosscheck batches using metadata only
validate complete primary coverage, batch size ceilings, and the global <=1.5D raw-assignment invariant before exposing raw evidence to any evaluator
materialize exactly one batch context packet
instantiate a fresh evaluator process and evaluate that primary batch exactly once
destroy that process and repeat with a fresh process for the next primary batch
repeat the same fresh-process isolation for every crosscheck batch
instantiate a fresh synthesis evaluator using only compact batch outputs
prohibited: recursive Gemini calls from within a batch evaluation
model-directed compute request loops that resend the same raw context
passing prior batch results into a later raw-evidence batch evaluator
whole-audit restart after a later batch failure
implicit overlap not represented in the validated batch plan
